title: The Great Rupert

evidence.note: Wikipedia states the film entered the public domain in 1978. That is a secondary claim. No Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volume or Copyright Office record was retrieved in this session, so non-renewal is not established here.

The recorded soundtrack of a sound film normally shares the film's own copyright status, so the score likely follows the print. Neither the print nor any separate score registration or renewal has been verified.
The underlying story, its earlier publication and any renewal of its copyright were not verified in this session.
In 2003, Fox and Legend Films released a colorized version titled A Christmas Wish. Colorization can carry its own copyright. A faithful copy of the black-and-white original adds none.

editorial:
The Great Rupert (1950) is an American comedy-fantasy produced by George Pal and directed by Irving Pichel, with Jimmy Durante, Tom Drake and Terry Moore. Eagle-Lion Films released it on March 1, 1950. Its title character is Rupert, an animated squirrel who helps two struggling families, and the Internet Archive describes him as a Christmas "guardian angel". A creator might want it for the Pal stop-motion squirrel work and its holiday setting.

The film is reported to have entered the public domain in 1978, which would mean its copyright was not renewed. This dossier could not confirm that from the renewal records, so treat the print as unverified until you check the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes and the Copyright Office catalog yourself. The practical trap is the 2003 colorized release from Fox and Legend Films, titled A Christmas Wish. The colorization may be protected separately, so source a black-and-white print instead. The status of the underlying story and the score is also unchecked.
faq: Is The Great Rupert free to use?

It is reported as being in the public domain since 1978, but this dossier did not verify that against the renewal records, and the story and score were not checked either. Check the 1977 to 1979 renewal records before relying on it.
Can I use the colorized A Christmas Wish version?
Not safely. The 2003 colorization released by Fox and Legend Films may carry its own copyright. Use a black-and-white copy of the original instead.
